Then, the software will perform several calculations. First, the guide RNA sequence is aligned to the control sequence in order to determine the position of the expected Cas9 break site. Next, in all Sanger sequence traces an alignment window is automatically selected that runs from 100 to 15 bp upstream of the break site. The sequence segment in this window of the experimental sample (and the optional reference) is aligned to that of the control in order to determine any offset between the sequence reads. Users may change the default settings for these calculations, which is necessary when alignment problems occur with these settings ( see Notes 6 and 7 ). Subsequently, two output plots are generated: one plot that can help with quality control and one that displays the indel/HDR spectrum.

steps.title: Isolate Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA from the following cell pools: a control pool (transfected with nuclease or guide RNA alone) and an experimental pool (exposed to both Cas9 and guide RNA). For TIDER, the experimental sample must also be co-transfected with the donor template.

steps.title: Amplify Target Region by PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify a region of approximately 500–1500 base pairs around the target site using PCR from the DNA of the control and experimental samples using primers that span the CRISPR target site.

steps.title: Generate Reference Sequence (TIDER only)
steps.instruction: Obtain a reference sequence that carries the desired base pair changes as designed in the donor template using one of two methods:

substeps.instruction: Method 1 (Site-directed mutagenesis): Use two overlapping mutated primers (reverse complements of each other) in combination with control primers. Perform a first PCR (primer a with mutated primer c, and mutated primer d with primer b). Denature and hybridize the resulting amplicons. Perform a second PCR using the annealing mixture as a template and control primers a and b, starting with an extension step followed by exponential amplification.

Method 2 (Synthetic DNA): Order synthesized DNA containing the designed mutations and the annealing sequences for the forward and reverse control primers (a, b). Amplify the synthesized fragment using primers a and b.

steps.title: Perform Sanger Sequencing
steps.instruction: Process the PCR products of the control, experimental sample, and (for TIDER) the reference sample using conventional Sanger sequencing to obtain sequence trace files in .ab1 or .scf format.

steps.title: Upload Data to TIDE/TIDER Tool
steps.instruction: Upload the .ab1 or .scf sequence trace files and a 20 nt character string representing the guide RNA sequence into the TIDE or TIDER web tool (http://tide.nki.nl or https://deskgen.com).

steps.title: Perform Quality Control Analysis
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the quality control plots to verify data integrity and alignment.

substeps.instruction: Confirm that the break site is located as expected.
Verify that the aberrant signal increases only around the break site and remains elevated downstream.
For TIDER, verify the presence of designed mutations by comparing the reference trace to the control trace and checking the relative incorporation of the donor template in the experimental sample.
Ensure R² > 0.9 and that aberrant signals upstream of the break site are below 10% for all files.

steps.title: Decompose Sequence Signal
steps.instruction: Perform decomposition of the mixed sequence signal in the experimental sample to estimate mutation frequencies.

substeps.instruction: For TIDE: Select a decomposition window downstream of the break site (larger windows increase robustness). Generate trace models for all possible indels of size 0 to n (default n=10) derived from the control trace and use non-negative linear modeling to determine the best combination of models.

For TIDER: Ensure the decomposition window covers the designed mutation location (default window is 100 bp). Generate simulations of all possible insertions and deletions from the control file and place them in a decomposition matrix with the control and reference to estimate incorporation frequency of template-directed mutations versus error-prone repair indels.
